title: arXiv Trending AI — Daily — 2026-11-02
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from a curated external shortlist and corroborating coverage, with limited citation evidence for papers this recent.

sections.title: Hybrid Computer Use: A Unified Programmatic, Semantic, and Visual Interface for General Agents
sections.abstract: HCU combines programmatic, accessibility-tree, and GUI interaction; on OSWorld 2.0, the authors report the highest Partial and Binary scores among compared systems and improved task success and efficiency across tested models.
sections.ranking_evidence: ArXiv TLDR's 2026-W45 curated shortlist placed it #2; it also appeared in Recursive Intelligence's 2026-11-02 AI/ML morning brief. Editorial coverage signals, not readership statistics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a three-channel interface with compact accessibility observations, batched actions, post-action diffs, and a skill for coordinating channels; evaluated models allocate work across them differently.
sections.unique_caveat: Performance claims are tied to OSWorld 2.0 and the tested models, platforms, and baselines; they do not establish gains for every application or workflow.

sections.title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
sections.abstract: ReuScope separates measurements of dataset overlap from performance-sensitivity tests in Capsule Vision 2024; removal of selected training rows lowered public-validation balanced accuracy from 82.5% to 61.2%, which the authors explicitly say is not an estimate of leakage-induced inflation.
sections.ranking_evidence: ArXiv TLDR's 2026-W45 shortlist placed it #3; the arXiv record notes acceptance at NeurIPS 2026, Track on Evaluations and Datasets. It spans AI and computer vision.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a paired audit protocol that distinguishes observed reuse from conditional performance sensitivity, specifying the evaluation population, class support, and uncertainty unit for each conclusion.
sections.unique_caveat: The audit covers one benchmark and one primary training pipeline; missing cross-recording patient identifiers prevent patient-level overlap counts, and reported intervals reflect seed variation rather than patient sampling.

sections.title: Context as Infrastructure: Knowledge Compilation for Retrieval in Agentic Systems with Harnesses
sections.abstract: The paper frames LLM-based knowledge compilation as an upstream supply layer for agentic retrieval; on FRAMES, claim-evidence trees reduced query tokens on average, while structural compilation did not produce a detectable accuracy gain under a competent harness.
sections.ranking_evidence: ArXiv TLDR's 2026-W45 shortlist placed it #4; it is cross-listed across information retrieval, AI, and language, and was surfaced by independent paper-summary services including EmergentMind and CatalyzeX.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe a configurable ingestion pipeline that compiles documents into structures such as claim-evidence trees, graphs, and timelines, and release RAGFlow; they distinguish context supply from retriever quality.
sections.unique_caveat: Measurements are one-benchmark, one-compiler-model operating points without confidence intervals or repeated seeds; FRAMES is English and Wikipedia-based, and the authors caution against generalizing the PageIndex result beyond that scale.

sections.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
sections.abstract: SecPO combines a loss based on an approximated injection-invariant reference with adversarially synthesized attacks; for Qwen3.6-27B, the authors report 8.8% AgentDojo attack success versus 78.8% for Meta-SecAlign under AttackerMovesSecond, with no noticeable utility reduction on nine evaluated benchmarks.
sections.ranking_evidence: ArXiv TLDR's 2026-W45 shortlist placed it #8. The authors provide a dedicated technical site and public code, training data, and model; security/AI cross-listing and artifact release corroborate technical relevance, not readership.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose SecPO to approximate an injection-invariant, utility-preserving reference and pair it with adversarial training against stronger synthesized injections; results are reported on specified adaptive attacks and benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline agent result is for one model and the specified AgentDojo attack setting; the abstract does not establish robustness to all real-world injection channels or adaptive attackers.

sections.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
sections.abstract: LSA hierarchically clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries can score clusters rather than all keys; the authors report faster attention at ultra-long context with similar measured accuracy, including one-layer speedups at 10M tokens.
sections.ranking_evidence: ArXiv TLDR's 2026-W45 shortlist placed it #9; separate paper-summary pages at EmergentMind and Papers.cool also surfaced the work. Reported 10M-token efficiency tests support technical relevance, not a claim about readership.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Distilled-LSA for adapting pretrained models and Native-LSA for next-token training, using hierarchical latent-space key clustering to reduce attention work at long context.
sections.unique_caveat: The large speed figures are per attention layer on a specified model at 10M tokens; Native-LSA is reported at 128k tokens, so these results do not establish end-to-end serving gains across model sizes or hardware.
